case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.name: get_current_conditions
events.content:

events.text:
**Short answer:** I'd go to Grand Haven, with Muskegon a close second. I expect pier salmon fishing to be slow at all four ports this week. These ratings are my own inference from water temperature. They are not based on fishing reports.

I had no DNR reports for this question, so I have no catch data, pier access information or lure details. The conditions tool also returned only a buoy summary for the week before 2024-07-30. It gave no modeled pierhead temperatures, no cold-layer depths and no wind forecast. So I can't see an upwelling signal or check wave risk.

**Ratings (0 slow to 4 excellent)**

| Port | Rating | Buoy surface temp last week (measured) |
|---|---|---|
| Grand Haven | 1 | avg 68 F, +1 F (buoy 45029) |
| Muskegon | 1 | avg 68 F, +1 F (buoy 45029) |
| South Haven | 0–1 | avg 71 F, +1 F (buoy 45168) |
| St. Joseph | 0–1 | avg 73 F, +2 F (buoy 45026) |

**Evidence**
- The buoys show surface water of 68–73 F, and it is rising slightly at every port.
- General guidance (NY DEC): Chinook and coho prefer 52–58 F, with an optimum of 53 F. At 68–73 F, salmon should be holding well below the surface.
- General guidance (Michigan Sea Grant / MSU Extension): north or east winds can cause upwelling, and a sharp drop in buoy surface temperature is the sign. Salmon move toward pierheads when that happens. The buoys show no drop this week. Each one is up 1–2 F.
- Buoy 45029 is shared by Grand Haven and Muskegon, so those two ports are indistinguishable on this data.

**My read**
- I'd expect salmon to be offshore in deeper, cooler water, out of reach of a pier. Without an upwelling, I'd expect few fish near the pierheads.
- The two northern ports have the coolest water. That gives them a slightly better chance if a north or east wind kicks up, so I put Grand Haven and Muskegon at 1.
- St. Joseph is the warmest and the least likely to hold salmon at the pier.
- Grand Haven is my pick because it is cool, and I'd guess it has a bit more pier access than Muskegon. That is a guess, and I have no report to back it.

**Caveats**
- Check the wind forecast before you go. A sustained north or east wind of about 15 mph or more for a day or two could turn things around. If you see the nearshore water temperature drop sharply, that is the time to go.
- If you want fish this week, a boat trolling at the thermocline depth gives a better chance than the pier. I couldn't get the cold-layer depth for this answer.
- I have no bulletin links because I didn't use any reports.
